findings.title: The EPFO ECR declares EPF wages of basic+DA while the contribution remitted was computed on the higher s.2(y) wage base — the file cannot reconcile
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_compute_slip (line ~968) computes the PF base as `_wb = wage_base.compute(...)` then `pf_wages = _wb.wages_paise + ot.pf_wages_paise`, and stores `pf_wages_paise` on the slip. domain/payroll/ecr.py::build_ecr (line ~239) IGNORES that stored column and re-derives `pf_wages = basic_paise + da_paise + one_time_pf_wages_paise`. I ran it: employee on basic 10,000 + HRA 18,000, FY 2026-27 month 6 → slip pf_wages_paise=1400000 (14,000, addback 4,000), pf_employee 1,680, employer EPS 1,166 / EPF 514; build_ecr emits EPF_WAGES=10000 with EPF_CONTRI=2194 and EPS=1166 — an implied contribution rate of 33.6% of the wages declared. The module's own comment two lines above warns "Omitting it here would file EPF wages lower than the 12% remitted against them, which the portal reconciles and rejects." No test in tests/test_epfo_ecr.py or tests/test_the_pf_wage_base_under_the_labour_codes.py asserts wages-vs-contribution consistency.
findings.ca_experience: Every employee whose basic+DA is below the ₹15,000 ceiling on a low-basic/high-HRA structure — the ordinary Indian structure at those salary levels — gets an ECR line the EPFO portal rejects, or accepts as a false wage declaration. The CA discovers it on the 15th, at the portal, after the run is finalised and the journal posted. The GL, the payslip and the challan say one number; the return says another.
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho Payroll generate the ECR from the same wage figure the contribution was computed on; the EPFO portal reconciles wages against contributions on upload and rejects the batch on a mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: In build_ecr, read `slip['pf_wages_paise'] + slip['one_time_pf_wages_paise']` (falling back to basic+da for pre-migration-334 slips where pf_wages_rule_applied is false/absent) instead of re-deriving. Add a test that asserts epf_contribution ≈ 12% of epf_wages for every member in the file.

verification.probe: ran wage_base.compute + _compute_pf: base 14,000, EPS 1,166 remitted, ECR declares 10,000

findings.title: 24Q Annexure II gives every employee the new-regime ₹75,000 standard deduction, including old-regime employees entitled to ₹50,000
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:form_24q_annexure_ii (line ~4407) passes `standard_deduction_paise=rates.new_regime_standard_deduction_paise` unconditionally. domain/payroll/annexure2.py:298 applies it as `standard_deduction_16_ia_paise=min(standard_deduction_paise, salary)` — the row carries `uses_new_regime` (set from the declaration) and consults it for professional tax (`allowable_professional_tax_paise`) but never for §16(ia). domain/income_tax/statutory_rates.py:142-143 holds new 75,000_00 / old 50,000_00 for FY 2025-26, carried to 2026-27. I ran build_annexure_ii with an old-regime declaration: `regime new? False, SD applied 7500000`. tests/test_24q_annexure_ii.py passes a single STD_DEDUCTION constant and never exercises the old regime.
findings.ca_experience: An old-regime employee's income under the head Salaries is understated by ₹25,000 on the annexure filed with Q4. TRACES generates Form 16 Part B from exactly this input, so the certificate is wrong in the employee's favour and traceable to the employer — the identical failure mode the module already fixed for §16(iii) professional tax and documented at annexure2.py:102-112.
findings.market_standard: Winman, ClearTax TDS and Saral TDS pick the §16(ia) figure from the regime flag carried on the Annexure II record, because the annexure has a 115BAC column and every deduction must be consistent with it.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass both figures into build_annexure_ii (or the FYTaxRates object) and select per row: `min(new if row.uses_new_regime else old, salary)`. Add a regime-parametrised test.

findings.title: The payslip PDF is headed with the CA FIRM's name, not the client company that actually employs the person
findings.evidence: services/payslip_pdf_service.py:278 `firm = _load_firm(run.get("firm_id") or firm_id)` and :377 `_load_firm` reads `db.table("firms").select("*").eq("id", firm_id)` — the accounting practice. build_payslip_pdf:114 then renders `firm_name = firm.get("name") or firm.get("firm_name") or "Employer"` as the document title. `run["client_id"]` is available on the same row and is never read. Same path is used by build_run_payslip_zip:330.
findings.ca_experience: Every payslip the bureau issues for every client is headed "<CA firm name>" instead of the employing company. A payslip is the employer's wage statement; handing an employee of Client X a slip branded with their accountant's name is not something a firm can send twice. It also leaks the CA firm's identity to every employee of every client.
findings.market_standard: BrightPay (the owner's own reference bureau product), greytHR and Zoho Payroll all print the EMPLOYER entity — name, address, PF/ESI registration numbers — on the payslip; the bureau's own branding appears nowhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Load the client row (client_name/legal_name, address, and the client_statutory_identity EPF/ESIC/PT registrations added by migration 325) and render that as the employer block. Keep the firm only as an optional "prepared by" footer.

findings.title: A draft payroll run that was never finalised is counted as TDS already deducted, months already paid and gross already paid in the next month's §192 projection
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_tds_already_deducted_this_fy (lines 700-753) reads `db.table("payroll_runs").select("id, month").eq(firm).eq(client)` with NO status filter, then sums `tds_paise`, counts months and sums `gross_paise` from those runs' slips. `_members_contributing_earlier_this_period` (lines 442-446) does the same for ESI Rule 50 coverage. By contrast _assemble_24q_source:4142 and form_24q_annexure_ii:4353 both filter `status in ("finalized","paid")`, and migration 323 draws the same line for RLS. There is no DELETE /runs/{id} and no recompute endpoint anywhere in routers/payroll.py, so an abandoned draft sits in the table permanently.
findings.ca_experience: A CA who creates a draft run for September to look at the numbers and then abandons it (there is no way to delete it) makes October, November and every later month under-withhold: `_months_remaining_for_spread` shortens, and the September draft's TDS is credited as if deposited. §192(1) makes the EMPLOYER liable for the shortfall and §201(1A) charges 1% a month on it. Nothing on the payslip looks wrong. Meanwhile the 24Q built from the same data excludes September, so the return and the withholding disagree.
findings.market_standard: greytHR and Zoho Payroll compute YTD tax credits from PROCESSED/approved payroll only; an unapproved run contributes nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `.in_("status", _PAYROLL_RELEASED)` to both reads, matching the 24Q/Annexure II/ECR/RLS line. Separately, add a way to discard or recompute a draft run.

findings.title: pt_applicable with no pt_state withholds zero professional tax and is reported as a gap by nothing — and the client-workspace form creates employees in exactly that state
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_compute_pt returns 0 for an unrecognised/empty state. _statutory_gaps (line 356) only appends when `classify_pt_state(...).is_gap`; I ran domain/payroll/professional_tax.classify_state(None) → `is_gap False, note 'No state set; no professional tax withheld.'`. domain/payroll/exceptions.py:123-130 uses the same classify_state, so the exception index misses it too. apps/web/app/clients/[id]/payroll/page.tsx:457-462 renders a `pt_applicable` checkbox and NEVER collects pt_state (the field does not appear in that form at all), and addEmployee (line 358) posts the payload straight through.
findings.ca_experience: A CA who adds an employee from the client workspace and ticks "PT" gets ₹0 professional tax withheld every month, forever, with no gap on the run, no line on the exception index, and nothing on the payslip. Article 276 makes the employer liable for the shortfall with interest. This is precisely the "a zero for Delhi and a zero for Gujarat are the same number meaning opposite things" failure the whole gap mechanism was built to prevent, reintroduced through the one form that does not collect the state.
findings.market_standard: greytHR and Zoho Payroll make the PT work-location mandatory before PT can be enabled on an employee.
findings.suggested_fix: Two changes: (a) classify_state must report `is_gap=True` when pt_applicable is set and the state is blank — the caller already knows pt_applicable; (b) add pt_state to the client-workspace employee form and refuse pt_applicable without it in EmployeeIn.

findings.title: The §10(13A) HRA salary base is annualised as this month × 12 regardless of how many months the employee actually works — a mid-year joiner's exemption computes to zero
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_compute_slip line ~1050 passes `basic_plus_da_paise=(basic + da) * 12` and `hra_received_paise=hra * 12` to _monthly_tds, while the income figure two lines above correctly uses `recurring * months_left + gross_already_paid_paise`. I ran it: an old-regime employee joining 1 Oct 2026 on basic ₹1,00,000 + 50% HRA, rent ₹1,20,000 for the six months — HRADetails with the 12-month base returns an exemption of ₹0 (rent 1.2L minus 10% of a fabricated 12L salary), with the correct 6-month base it returns ₹60,000.
findings.ca_experience: Every mid-year joiner on the old regime who claims HRA loses their entire §10(13A) exemption in the withholding, because the "rent paid less 10% of salary" limb is computed against twice the salary they will earn. On the worked figures that is ~₹18,700 over-withheld across six months, recoverable only on assessment a year later — the same class of error, and the same direction, as the twelve-month projection bug the 1 September audit fixed. The mid-year raise case is wrong the same way.
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho Payroll compute the §10(13A) limbs on the salary and HRA for the period the rent relates to, per Rule 2A.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `(basic + da) * months_employed_in_fy` and `hra * months_employed_in_fy`, or better, accumulate actual paid basic/DA/HRA from the year's slips plus the projected remainder — the same shape annual_gross already uses.

findings.title: §17(2) perquisites are valued, stored and reported on Form 16 but never enter the monthly §192 withholding
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_compute_slip builds `annual_gross = gross_already_paid + recurring*months_left + ot.taxable_paise` (line ~1035) — payroll_perquisites is never read there, and `_compute_slip` has no perquisite parameter. The table IS read by form_24q_annexure_ii:4390 (`db.table("payroll_perquisites")`) and lands in `perquisites_17_2_paise` on the annexure. domain/payroll/perquisites.py values accommodation, car, concessional loan, meals and gifts under Rule 3.
findings.ca_experience: An employee with a company car or employer accommodation has the perquisite on their Form 16 and no tax withheld against it all year. The whole year's tax on the perquisite lands as a demand on the employee at assessment, and under §192(1) the shortfall is the employer's — with §201(1A) interest at 1% a month. The CA sees a correct Annexure II and a payslip that never mentioned it.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Payroll, greytHR and Keka add the monthly perquisite value into the projected annual salary for §192 and show it as a separate non-cash earning line on the payslip.
findings.suggested_fix: Read payroll_perquisites once per run (like _declarations_for_run) and add the year's value to annual_gross in _compute_slip, with the month's proportionate share shown on the payslip as a non-cash perquisite.

findings.title: Reversing a payroll run does not restore employee loan balances, so re-finalising the same run recovers the instalment twice
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:finalize_run:2314 calls `_apply_loan_recoveries(db, firm_id, client_id, run_id)` after the journal posts; that function (line 568) reduces `payroll_loans.outstanding_paise` by each slip's `loan_recovery_paise` and closes the loan at zero. reverse_run (line 2431) reverses both journals and resets status/journal ids — it never touches payroll_loans and never mentions them. The slips are not deleted, so a second finalize_run re-reads the same `loan_recovery_paise` and applies it again. The docstring of _apply_loan_recoveries explicitly reasons that finalisation "is guarded against running twice" — reverse_run removes that guard.
findings.ca_experience: A CA who reverses August to correct something and re-finalises has written the employee's advance down twice. The loan closes early, the employee is shown a nil balance they still owe, and the ledger's Employee Loans receivable is understated by the instalment. Nothing on any screen says it happened.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Payroll and greytHR reverse loan/advance amortisation entries when a payroll run is rolled back.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the inverse write to reverse_run (add the recovered amount back and clear closed_on), or make the write-down idempotent by recording the run_id against each loan repayment rather than mutating a running balance.

findings.title: /payroll/reports recomputes employer PF on basic alone and ESI without Rule 50 — the four exact drifts the statutory page was rewritten to remove, in a CSV the CA hands to the client
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx:617-628 `buildCtcRows`: `employerPf = Math.min(Math.round((emp.basic_paise * 12) / 100), 180000)` (12% of BASIC only, ignoring DA, ignoring the s.2(y) base, ignoring eps_eligible) and `employerEsi = emp.esi_applicable && s.gross_paise <= 2100000 ? Math.round((s.gross_paise * 325) / 10000) : 0` (current-month ceiling test, no contribution period). The slip already stores `pf_employer_paise` and `esi_employer_paise` and they are not read. Exported at line 650 with the header "Employee,PAN,Gross Salary,Employer PF (12%),Employer ESI (3.25%),Total CTC". apps/web/app/payroll/statutory/page.tsx:1-27 documents these very four drifts as removed; apps/web/scripts/statutory-files-are-server-built.test.ts guards only app/payroll/page.tsx, not this file.
findings.ca_experience: The CTC report and its CSV disagree with the payslip, the ledger and the PF challan for every employee with a DA component, every employee excluded from EPS under GSR 609(E), and every employee whose wages crossed ₹21,000 mid-period. It also omits EDLI and the admin charge, which migration 329 established are part of the employer's cost. A CA who quotes a client their staff cost from this screen quotes the wrong number.
findings.market_standard: Every payroll product derives CTC from the stored employer contribution on the processed payslip, not from a re-derivation in the reporting layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Read pf_employer_paise, esi_employer_paise, edli_paise and pf_admin_paise off the slip; delete buildCtcRows' arithmetic. Extend statutory-files-are-server-built.test.ts to cover app/payroll/reports/page.tsx.

findings.title: The TDS projection screen computes §192 in TypeScript with hardcoded FY 2025-26 new-regime rates, no old regime, no declarations and no §192(3)
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/services/payrollTdsEstimate.ts hardcodes the FY2025-26 slabs, the ₹75,000 standard deduction and the ₹12,00,000 §87A ceiling as literals, is explicitly "deliberately NOT FY-versioned", and its own header calls itself "a standing CLAUDE.md violation tracked as roadmap R2.10". apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx:32 imports it and lines 753-761/787 use it: `estimatedMonthlyGross = basic + round(basic*hra%/100) + round(basic*da%/100) + other_allowances` — which also omits lta_paise, medical_paise and special_allowance_paise, a third definition of gross.
findings.ca_experience: The TDS Projection tab shows an old-regime employee with a home loan and HRA a projected annual tax computed as if they were on the new regime with nothing declared, on a gross that excludes three of their salary components. It will disagree with the payslip, and in FY 2027-28 it will silently still be applying FY 2025-26 slabs because it has no FY registry.
findings.market_standard: greytHR and Zoho Payroll show a tax-projection worksheet generated by the same engine that computes the payslip, per regime, with the employee's declarations in it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a server endpoint that returns the projection from _monthly_tds / decl_domain.withholding_tax_paise for the selected employee and month, then delete payrollTdsEstimate.ts.

findings.title: Seven finished backend capabilities have no screen anywhere — including the leaver settlement and the Annexure II that produces Form 16
findings.evidence: I grepped apps/web/{app,components,lib} for each endpoint path. Zero occurrences of: `settlement/record` and `employees/{id}/settlement` (routers/payroll.py:5179, 5233 — F&F), `arrears-relief` (:5457, §89/Form 10E), `perquisites` (:5561, :5649 — Rule 3 valuation and recording), `salary-revisions` (:5733, :5798), `payroll/employees/.../loans` (:5827, :5889), `24q-annexure-ii` (:4308), `salary-structures/{id}/apply` (:1551). Confirmed against `grep -o 'api\.payroll\.[a-zA-Z]*'` over the whole app: the UI calls 30 of the router's ~55 endpoints.
findings.ca_experience: A CA cannot settle a leaver, record a salary revision, record an advance, value a perquisite, compute §89 relief, apply a salary structure, or produce the Annexure II from any screen in the product. docs/audits/2026-09-01-payroll-can-it-run-a-year.md answers its own question "yes for the monthly cycle, the leaver and the statutory returns" — the leaver and the year-end are not reachable. Every one of them is a task the CA must do somewhere else, which defeats the whole pitch.
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho Payroll all ship exit/F&F, salary revision with arrears, loans with EMI, and a Form 16 / Annexure II export as first-class screens.
findings.suggested_fix: Prioritise by what a year needs: (1) Annexure II on the client Outputs shelf (it is the year-end deliverable), (2) settlement on the employee drawer, (3) salary revisions + apply-structure on Inputs, (4) loans, (5) perquisites, (6) §89.

findings.title: PATCH /employees silently discards joining_date, and the edit form sends it — so a wrong joining date can never be corrected
findings.evidence: models/payroll.py:EmployeeUpdateIn (lines 146-172) lists date_of_birth but NOT joining_date, eps_eligible or gratuity_act_covered. Pydantic v2 ignores extra keys by default; I ran `EmployeeUpdateIn(name='A', joining_date='2026-10-01', eps_eligible=False).model_dump(exclude_none=True)` → `{'name': 'A'}`. apps/web/components/payroll/AddEmployeeModal.tsx:113 puts `joining_date` in the payload and line 122 calls `api.payroll.updateEmployee(...)` on edit. routers/payroll.py:update_employee:1433 does `data.model_dump(exclude_none=True)` and writes whatever survived. apps/web/scripts/employee-form-captures-what-filing-needs.test.ts asserts joining_date is in the form — and passes, while the edit does nothing.
findings.ca_experience: A CA who notices an employee's joining date is wrong opens the edit form, changes it, sees "saved", and nothing changes. joining_date drives `_months_employed_in_fy` (a mid-year joiner over-deducted by ₹1,46,250 in the audit's own worked example) and the entire gratuity computation. Same for eps_eligible, which decides whether a GSR 609(E)-excluded member gets a pension contribution on the ECR.
findings.market_standard: Every payroll product allows date-of-joining correction with an audit trail.
findings.suggested_fix: Add joining_date, eps_eligible and gratuity_act_covered to EmployeeUpdateIn. Separately, consider `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')` on the payroll input models so a dropped field is a 422 rather than silence.

findings.title: The client workspace's own employee form collects neither PAN, joining date, UAN, ESIC number, bank details, PT state, DA, LTA, medical nor special allowance
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/payroll/page.tsx:433-465 — the New Employee form has exactly: Name, Employee Code, Date of Birth, Designation, Department, Basic, HRA %, Aadhaar, and PF/ESI/PT checkboxes. apps/web/components/payroll/AddEmployeeModal.tsx (used on /payroll/people) has the complementary set: PAN, gender, DA %, other allowances, PT state, UAN, ESIC, joining date, bank — and no date of birth and no employee code. Neither captures lta_paise, medical_paise or special_allowance_paise, which _compute_slip pays (routers/payroll.py:936-940) and register.py prints.
findings.ca_experience: An employee added from the client workspace — which docs/architecture/10-payroll.md declares the canonical surface — is immediately blocked on the ECR (no UAN), the ESIC return (no IP), the 24Q (no PAN, §206AA), the bank advice (no account) and is over-deducted under §192 (no joining date). The CA must then find the other form, on a different screen, to finish the record. And no form anywhere can set LTA, medical or special allowance except a CSV import.
findings.market_standard: greytHR/Keka/Zoho onboarding wizards collect statutory identity, bank and the full CTC breakup in one flow, and refuse to activate an employee whose statutory fields are blank.
findings.suggested_fix: One employee form, used by both surfaces — the design doc already says "one employee form". Fold AddEmployeeModal into the client workspace and add DOB, employee code, LTA/medical/special.

findings.title: A leaver's settlement TDS never reaches the quarterly 24Q, though it does reach the annual Annexure II — so Annexure I and Annexure II disagree
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_assemble_24q_source (lines 4136-4165) builds slips_by_month purely from `payroll_runs` → `payroll_slips`; `payroll_settlements` is never queried. form_24q_annexure_ii:4380-4400 DOES read payroll_settlements and adds `settled['tds_paise']` to the annual TDS. record_settlement:5330 computes and stores a §192 withholding on the settlement (`tds` column) and posts it to TDS Payable - Salary via journal_for_settlement. docs/audits/2026-09-01-payroll-can-it-run-a-year.md claims "its TDS reaches 24Q".
findings.ca_experience: A CA who settles a leaver in, say, November deposits the TDS on the challan but files Q3's 24Q short by that amount. The challan will not reconcile against the deductee rows, and the employee gets no 26AS credit for the deduction until the Q4 Annexure II — which will then show a TDS total larger than the sum of the four quarters' Annexure I. TRACES flags this as a short-deduction default.
findings.market_standard: Winman TDS, ClearTax and Saral build Annexure I from every deduction in the quarter, terminal payments included.
findings.suggested_fix: In _assemble_24q_source, read payroll_settlements for the quarter's months and emit a deductee row per settlement (payment_date = leaving/payment date, amount = taxable_paise, tds = tds_paise), joined to the same PAN checks.

findings.title: Attendance and LOP cannot be entered from the client Payroll tab at all — they live on a firm-wide screen filed under the Team rail
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/payroll/page.tsx has five tabs (Inputs/Register/Release/Outputs/Setup, line 1724) and the string "attendance" appears only in comments and in the run-gap banner — no editor. The only attendance editor is apps/web/app/payroll/attendance/page.tsx, which is linked from apps/web/components/panels/TeamPanel.tsx:33 (`/payroll/attendance`, label "Attendance") and from nowhere in the payroll pages; apps/web/app/payroll/page.tsx links only to People, Declarations and Reports. docs/architecture/10-payroll.md specifies Inputs as "LOP, joiners, leavers, revisions effective this month".
findings.ca_experience: The CA opens the client's Payroll tab on the 3rd, is told by the run banner that nobody entered attendance for eleven employees, and there is no control on that screen to enter it. They must leave the client workspace, open the Team rail, find Attendance, pick the client from a dropdown, and come back. LOP is the single input that moves every rupee on every payslip.
findings.market_standard: In greytHR/Keka/Zoho the LOP/attendance input sits inside the payroll month, immediately before Process.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the attendance editor (and one-time earnings, which is on the same page) into the client workspace Inputs tab, scoped to that client-month; keep a firm-wide view if wanted, but not as the only door.

findings.title: Both firm-level payroll screens load every payslip of every run the firm has ever produced into the browser
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/payroll/page.tsx:874-877 — `await Promise.all(runList.map(r => api.payroll.getRunSlips(r.id)))`: one HTTP round trip per run, for every run of every client, on page mount, even though the default Month tab does not use `slips` (only the Statutory Returns tab does). apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx:1230-1233 — `sb.from("payroll_slips").select("*").in("run_id", runIds)` with runIds = every run in the firm, in a PostgREST URL. CLAUDE.md: "No report may fetch rows proportional to transaction volume… what crosses the wire must be proportional to the size of the ANSWER."
findings.ca_experience: At the target beachhead of 15-60 clients with 3-12 payroll clients each and two years of history, /payroll makes hundreds of sequential Singapore→Mumbai round trips before rendering, and /payroll/reports puts hundreds of UUIDs into a single URL. lib/api aborts at 45 seconds and the abort is deliberately never retried, so the screen simply fails — the same shape as the 54-second cash-flow report CLAUDE.md documents.
findings.market_standard: N/A — this is an architectural rule the codebase already states and enforces elsewhere (account_period_balances, public.cash_flow_report).
findings.suggested_fix: Server-side aggregates: a `/reports/*` endpoint per tab returning finished rows for one client-month or one FY, and lazy-load the Statutory Returns tab's data only when that tab is opened.

findings.title: Annual professional tax for §16(iii) is estimated as this month's PT × 12 — six times the year's real liability in a Tamil Nadu September, zero in every other month
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:_compute_slip line ~1053 passes `professional_tax_paise=pt * 12`. _compute_pt_tn (line 283) returns the whole half-yearly amount in months 9 and 3 and zero otherwise; _compute_pt_mh returns ₹300 in February and ₹200 otherwise. I ran an old-regime TN employee on ₹50,000 basic: month 8 pt=0 tds=₹6,110; month 9 pt=₹1,250 tds=₹5,850; month 10 pt=0 tds=₹6,110 — September claims ₹15,000 of §16(iii) against a real annual PT of ₹2,500.
findings.ca_experience: An old-regime employee in Tamil Nadu has their TDS drop by ~₹260 in September and March and revert in between, because the deduction claimed is 6× the year's actual PT. Maharashtra's February is wrong the same way. Under the new regime it is masked because §115BAC(2) disallows §16(iii) entirely — so this only surfaces on old-regime employees, where it produces a month-to-month TDS wobble a CA cannot explain.
findings.market_standard: greytHR and Zoho project the ANNUAL PT liability for the state (₹2,500 MH, ₹2,500 TN, ₹2,400 KA/WB) and hold it constant across the year's projection.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the year's PT by summing _compute_pt over the twelve months of the FY for that employee's state (cheap, pure) and pass that, rather than the month × 12.

findings.title: `logger` is undefined in the /employee-exceptions error path — a failed declarations read raises NameError from inside the except
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:3478 `logger.exception("could not read declarations for the exception index")`. The module defines only `_logger = logging.getLogger("caflow.payroll")` at line 74; I parsed the module's AST and confirmed no assignment named `logger` exists. It sits inside `except Exception:` guarding the payroll_it_declarations read at line 3471. This is the same defect docs/audits/2026-09-01 recorded as finding 3 and claimed fixed and "pinned by tests that force a read to fail" — reintroduced.
findings.ca_experience: On the one day the declarations table is unreachable, the exception index does not degrade to "nobody intimated the old regime" as designed — it 500s. The CA loses the screen that tells them which employees will block the ECR, ESIC return and 24Q, at exactly the moment something is already wrong.
findings.market_standard: N/A — a defensive-path defect.
findings.suggested_fix: `_logger.exception(...)`. Add a lint rule or a test that forces this read to fail, as the earlier fix did for the other five branches.

findings.title: The payroll module's own statutory calendar contradicts compliance_engine: it invents a PT due date the backend deliberately refuses, and omits the three deposit dates that actually attract interest
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx:222-236 emits a monthly "PT Challan" due on the last day of the month, described as "Maharashtra: ₹200 if > ₹10,000", for every client. tests/test_payroll_deposit_due_dates.py:63 `test_professional_tax_is_deliberately_absent` and tests/test_payroll_owes_three_deposits_a_month.py:93 pin that compliance_engine refuses to state a PT due date because it is per-state. The calendar has no row at all for the EPF deposit (15th), the ESI deposit (15th) or the monthly TDS deposit (7th, 30 April for March) which services/compliance_engine.py:279-326 computes and which reach /deadlines through compliance_obligation_service.py:312. apps/web/app/payroll/page.tsx:70-127 carries a second, differently-wrong copy: in January (m=0) it shows only "TDS 24Q Q4 due 31 May" and omits the Q3 return due 31 January. It also asserts a half-yearly ESI return due 11 Nov / 11 May, which the backend does not model (I could not establish from primary sources in this session whether that return still exists — low confidence on that limb specifically).
findings.ca_experience: Two calendars in one product give different answers. A Karnataka client is told PT is due on the last day of the month (it is the 20th of the following month); a Tamil Nadu client is told it is monthly (it is half-yearly). In January the payroll landing page shows no 24Q deadline for the quarter that closed on 31 December. And the deposits that carry §201(1A) interest at 1.5% a month are not on the payroll calendar at all.
findings.market_standard: Every Indian compliance product derives the calendar from one rules table; Saral and ClearTax hold state-wise PT due dates explicitly rather than assuming one.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both TypeScript calendars and render compliance_engine.payroll_deposit_due_dates plus the 24Q dates through an endpoint. Keep PT's absence visible as a named refusal, the way statutory_gaps does — not as an invented date.

findings.title: /statutory-position computes PF on basic+DA, not the s.2(y) wage base the payroll run uses, so the projection disagrees with the payslip
findings.evidence: routers/payroll.py:statutory_position line ~4972: `pf = _compute_pf(basic + da, fy, eps_eligible=...)`. _compute_slip line 968 uses `wage_base.compute(...)` and passes `_wb.wages_paise + ot.pf_wages_paise`. domain/payroll/wage_base.py:WAGE_RULE_EFFECTIVE_FROM = 2025-11-21, so every month from November 2025 onward is governed and today is 2026-09-07.
findings.ca_experience: The Statutory Deductions screen — the one the CA opens to see PF liability and gratuity provision per employee — understates employer and employee PF for every employee on a low-basic/high-HRA structure below the ceiling. It will not tie to the payslip, the ledger or the challan, and the screen exists specifically because a TypeScript version of it had drifted the same way.
findings.market_standard: N/A — internal consistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Call wage_base.compute in statutory_position with the same components and month, and surface pf_wages_addback_paise so a CA can see why the base differs from basic+DA.

findings.title: A payroll run cannot be recomputed or discarded — reversal reopens it at 'review' with the original frozen slips
findings.evidence: The router exposes no DELETE /runs/{id} and no recompute endpoint (verified by reading the full @router index of routers/payroll.py). create_run:1745 409s if a run exists for (firm, client, month). reverse_run:2489 sets status back to 'review' and its docstring says "so it can be corrected and re-finalized" — but the payroll_slips rows are untouched, so re-finalising posts the same numbers. _release_gaps:2126 even tells the CA to "Regenerate the run to find out", an action that does not exist.
findings.ca_experience: Attendance arrives after a draft was created; the CA enters it; nothing recomputes. The put_attendance guard (line 3021) refuses to change attendance under a released run and says "Reverse the run first" — but reversing does not let the figures change either. The only escape is a manual database edit. And the abandoned draft then corrupts the next month's §192 (see PAY-04).
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho all allow a payroll to be un-processed and re-run before it is locked, and support an off-cycle correction run after.
findings.suggested_fix: Add POST /runs/{id}/recompute (draft/review only) that deletes and rebuilds the slips through the same path create_run uses, and DELETE /runs/{id} for an unfinalised run.

findings.title: §80CCD(2)'s 14%/10% cap is applied to gross salary instead of basic+DA, so a large employer-NPS declaration can be over-allowed
findings.evidence: domain/income_tax/itr_engine.py:328 `salary_base_80ccd2 = req.salary_for_80ccd2_paise if not None else req.gross_salary_paise`, and the comment at :192 states the cap base is "salary (basic + DA)". domain/payroll/declarations.py:_build_request accepts `salary_for_80ccd2_paise` but routers/payroll.py never passes it — I grepped: the only occurrences of `salary_for_80ccd2` in the repo are in declarations.py and itr_engine.py.
findings.ca_experience: An employee who declares an employer NPS contribution under §80CCD(2) is allowed up to 14% of GROSS rather than 14% of basic+DA. On a 40%-basic structure that is more than double the statutory cap, and it under-withholds — a §192(1) shortfall the employer answers for. It binds only where the declared NPS figure is large, so it will not show up on most employees.
findings.market_standard: greytHR and Zoho compute the §80CCD(2) cap on basic+DA per the Explanation to §80CCD.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `salary_for_80ccd2_paise=(basic + da) * months_employed_in_fy` from _compute_slip through _monthly_tds into the declaration request.

findings.title: Statutory bonus is computed only inside a leaver's settlement — there is no annual bonus run for continuing employees
findings.evidence: domain/payroll/bonus.py implements §2(13)/§8/§10/§11/§12 correctly and completely. Its only caller in the whole backend is routers/payroll.py:5112, inside `_compose_settlement`. Grep for `bonus_domain` / `bonus.compute` across routers/ and services/ returns exactly that one line.
findings.ca_experience: The Payment of Bonus Act makes bonus a debt payable within eight months of the accounting year's close (§19) to every employee drawing ≤₹21,000. A CA running a client's payroll on this cannot compute or pay the annual bonus for anyone still employed — only for people who leave. They fall back to a spreadsheet for the one statutory annual payment the module already knows how to compute.
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho Payroll all run an annual statutory-bonus computation across the roster with a Form C / Form D register.
findings.suggested_fix: An annual bonus run: compute bonus_domain over the eligible roster for an accounting year, produce Form C, and pay it through the one-time-earnings path (kind='bonus') so it lands correctly for PF/ESI/§17(1).

findings.title: Leave is half-built: balances are invented in TypeScript as 12/12/15, nothing accrues or carries forward, and the employee portal shows the invented figure
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/payroll/attendance/page.tsx:311-315 `casual_leave_balance: existing?.casual_leave_balance ?? 12, sick_leave_balance: ... ?? 12, earned_leave_balance: ... ?? 15` — three literals with no policy behind them. Line 604 upserts them into `leave_balances`. apps/web/app/portal/employee/page.tsx:226 reads leave_balances and renders it to the employee. No backend module touches leave_balances (grep across apps/api returns only migrations 027/041/074/261/262/297 — grants and RLS, no logic). docs/architecture/10-payroll.md lists "Leave management" under Deferred.
findings.ca_experience: An employee opens the portal and is told they have 12 casual, 12 sick and 15 earned days — a number no firm set and no policy supports, written into the database by whoever last pressed Save on the attendance screen. That is worse than showing nothing: it is an entitlement statement the employer did not make. Leave encashment on settlement still has to be typed in by hand.
findings.market_standard: greytHR/Keka/Zoho hold a leave policy per client with accrual rules, carry-forward caps, encashment and apply/approve — or, if not built, show nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the invented defaults and the portal leave tab until a policy model exists (the honest option, matching the module's own gap discipline), or build a per-client leave policy with accrual server-side.

findings.title: The payroll journal posts one Salaries Expense account and defines the debit as the sum of the credits
findings.evidence: services/phase2_journal_service.py:_build_payroll_lines:813-890 — a single `%Salaries Expense%` debit whose amount is the sum of net + PF (incl. EDLI and admin) + ESI + PT + TDS + loans, with the docstring conceding "Employer PF/ESI is folded into Salaries Expense here… A future enhancement could split it into a dedicated 'Contribution to PF & Other Funds' account for the Schedule III employee-benefit sub-classification". docs/audits/2026-09-01 itself warns that "defining the debit as the sum of the credits is exactly how the payroll accrual's own missing-credit-leg bug stayed hidden" — and the accrual still does it.
findings.ca_experience: Schedule III requires Employee benefits expense split into (a) salaries and wages, (b) contribution to provident and other funds, (c) staff welfare. This product produces a trial balance that cannot be mapped to that note without manual analysis, in a platform whose whole pitch is that payroll posts into the ledger the CA already closes. And a missing credit leg is undetectable by construction, because the debit is derived from the credits.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime and Zoho Books post salaries, employer PF, employer ESI and staff welfare to separate ledgers so Schedule III maps directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into Salaries and Wages / Contribution to PF and Other Funds (employer PF + EPS + EDLI + admin) / Contribution to ESI, compute the debit independently from the slip components, and let the kernel's balance assertion catch a disagreement.

findings.title: The employee portal shows a payslip list and a leave number and nothing else a self-service portal is bought for
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/portal/employee/page.tsx (482 lines) has tabs for payslips (list + PDF download via api.payroll.downloadPayslip) and leave balances; components/portal/TaxDeclarationTab.tsx lets an employee file a declaration by writing payroll_it_declarations directly through PostgREST. There is no TDS working, no Form 12BB output, no Form 16 access, no reimbursement claim, no leave apply/approve, no proof upload against a declaration line (`proof_reference` is a free-text string on the item, with no document attached). docs/architecture/10-payroll.md specifies "Employee portal → Pay: Payslip, how your TDS was arrived at, Form 12BB, Form 16".
findings.ca_experience: The firm's support burden does not move. Every "why is my TDS this much", "send me my Form 16", "here is my rent receipt" still arrives by WhatsApp — which is the specific thing the product is meant to replace. The investment-proof workflow has no place to put a proof.
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho ESS: payslip, tax worksheet showing the projection line by line, IT declaration with a proof-upload window and CA verification, Form 16 download, reimbursement claims, leave apply/approve.
findings.suggested_fix: Start with the TDS working (the server already has every input in _monthly_tds) and proof upload against a declaration item — the two that remove the most WhatsApp.

findings.title: No bank advice file, no payslip delivery, no reimbursements or flexible benefits, no overtime or shift, no month-on-month variance, no department cost or headcount analytics
findings.evidence: Grepped the whole backend: no NEFT/bank-advice generator (domain/payroll/register.py carries bank_account_no and bank_ifsc columns but there is no per-bank format module); no email/WhatsApp path for payslips — services/payslip_pdf_service.py only returns bytes and build_run_payslip_zip a zip. models/payroll.py OneTimeEarningsIn kinds are incentive|bonus|ex_gratia|arrears|commission|reimbursement|other with no overtime, shift or flexible-benefit-plan modelling. apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx has six tabs (payslip summary, YTD, CTC, TDS projection, year-end, calendar) — no variance-vs-last-month and no department/headcount analytics, despite `department` being on the employee master and in the register. docs/architecture/10-payroll.md defers bank advice deliberately.
findings.ca_experience: After finalising, the CA still exports to Excel to build the bank file, and still emails thirty payslips by hand. The owner's stated goal is analytics that make CAs "addicted" — there is no cross-client payroll analytics anywhere, and the client-level reports do not answer the first question anyone asks on the 3rd: "why is this month bigger than last month, and by whom?" (the run stores total_one_time_paise, which is the beginning of that answer and is not surfaced as a variance).
findings.market_standard: greytHR/Keka/Zoho ship per-bank advice templates, payslip email/WhatsApp, reimbursement and FBP modules, overtime and shift, and a payroll register with month-on-month variance and department-wise cost as standard.
findings.suggested_fix: Highest value per unit of work, in order: (1) month-on-month variance on the Register tab (data already stored), (2) payslip email from the zip path, (3) a generic NEFT CSV plus two or three bank formats, (4) department-wise cost from the register. Keep bank advice as prepare-only, consistent with the never-move-client-money rule.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Bank advice, month-on-month variance, department cost/headcount analytics and overtime/shift are genuinely absent (domain/payroll/register.py:59-60 has the bank columns with no consumer; apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx has six tabs and no occurrence of 'department'; payroll_runs.total_one_time_paise at migration 331:217 is returned at routers/payroll.py:4492 and never differenced). But reimbursements ARE modelled — models/payroll.py:509 plus domain/payroll/one_time_earnings.py:81-111 give a reimbursement kind the correct non-salary §17(1) treatment — and payslip DELIVERY exists as employee self-service (apps/web/app/portal/employee/page.tsx:116-123, invited by services/employee_portal_service.py:144-199); what is missing there is emailing the PDF and bulk invites, not a route to the employee. Severity stays medium: these are market-standard absences, not wrong numbers.
verification.probe: grep -rni 'neft|bank advice|bank_advice' over apps/api --include=*.py/*.sql printed only payment_mode enums, migration 161 prose and bank-narration tests — no advice-file builder. grep -rn 'TabsTrigger' apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx printed six triggers (payslip-summary, ytd, ctc, tds-projection, year-end, statutory-calendar). grep -rn 'department' on the same file printed nothing. grep -rli overtime apps/api/migrations/ printed nothing.

lens_notes.literal: Four of the six sub-claims hold. Bank advice: no generator anywhere — grep for neft/bank advice across apps/api returns only payment_mode enums and bank-narration parsing; domain/payroll/register.py:59-60 carries 'Bank Account'/'Bank IFSC' columns in the salary-register CSV and nothing consumes them. Month-on-month variance: absent — the only 'variance' in apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx:873-896 is projected-vs-actual TDS, a different comparison; grep 'variance' over routers/payroll.py and domain/payroll/*.py returns nothing. Department analytics: 'department' reaches register.py:36 and the slip selects at routers/payroll.py:1978,2538,2576, and there is zero occurrence of 'department' in apps/web/app/payroll/reports/page.tsx. Overtime/shift: no column, no kind, no migration (grep -rli overtime over apps/api/migrations returns nothing; the four hits in domain/payroll are prose in bonus.py/wage_base.py/gratuity.py explaining what is EXCLUDED). Reports tabs: exactly six TabsTrigger at reports/page.tsx:1312-1329. TWO sub-claims are wrong. (a) 'no reimbursements' — reimbursement is a modelled OneTimeEarningsIn kind (models/payroll.py:509) with correct §17(1) treatment in domain/payroll/one_time_earnings.py:70,81-111 (_NON_SALARY_KINDS = {'reimbursement'}, not PF/ESI/taxable). What is missing is a CLAIM workflow and an FBP declaration, not the earning type. (b) 'no payslip delivery' overstates it: apps/web/app/portal/employee/page.tsx:61,101-123 is an employee self-service portal whose default tab is payslips and which downloads the PDF, provisioned by services/employee_portal_service.py:144-199 (invite_employee sends 'Your payslip portal access'). What is absent is emailing/WhatsApping the PDF itself and bulk invites.
lens_notes.guards: None that close the gaps. docs/architecture/10-payroll.md:389-391 defers bank advice explicitly ('a per-bank format zoo that grows per client... the payment is the client's act anyway') and :398 puts 'shift rostering' under 'Deliberately not built' — but the same document's own current-status header at :22 says the bank-advice deferral is 'no longer current' and 'comes back into scope under depth'. CLAUDE.md records no decision on any of these six, so the architecture doc is the only authority and it is self-contradictory on bank advice. Design doc :168 specifies 'variance against the last approved month' on the Register tab as intended, which makes the variance gap a shortfall against the product's own spec rather than a deliberate omission.
lens_notes.reach: All reachable and live. /payroll/reports is a real page linked from app/payroll/page.tsx:942, the register CSV endpoint is wired at lib/api/index.ts:1315-1318, and payroll_runs.total_one_time_paise exists (migration 331_a_month_is_not_a_pure_repeat.sql:217) and is already returned to the client at routers/payroll.py:4492 — so the variance the finding wants is one subtraction away from data already on the wire.

findings.title: Payroll is a link inside the Accounting rail and its screens are split across three top-level areas
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/panels/AccountingPanel.tsx:44,46 lists "Payroll" → /payroll and "Payroll Statutory" → /payroll/statutory. apps/web/components/panels/TeamPanel.tsx:33 lists "/payroll/attendance" under Team. apps/web/lib/workspace/workspaceConfig.ts:176 maps `/payroll*` into the "accounting" workspace. /payroll/people, /payroll/declarations and /payroll/reports appear in no panel — they are reachable only from buttons on /payroll (app/payroll/page.tsx:933-943). docs/architecture/10-payroll.md specifies "Payroll becomes the 13th top-level workspace" with six sections including a Setup screen that publishes state coverage — /payroll/setup does not exist (there is no such directory under apps/web/app/payroll).
findings.ca_experience: A bureau running payroll for a dozen clients has no home screen for the service they sell. The firm-level PT/LWF state-coverage screen the design calls "our largest liability turned into the one claim no competitor makes" is not built — GET /statutory-values and PUT /statutory-values/pt exist in lib/api (index.ts:622-636) with no page calling them, so the firm-recorded-PT-slabs mechanism that makes bundling survivable cannot be used.
findings.market_standard: Payroll is a top-level module in every product in this category.
findings.suggested_fix: Promote /payroll to its own workspace with Month · People · Declarations · Statutory · Reports · Setup, move Attendance out of Team, and build the Setup screen over the statutory-values endpoints that already exist.

verification.what_is_actually_true: The navigation is split as described (AccountingPanel.tsx:44-46, TeamPanel.tsx:33, workspaceConfig.ts:175) and /payroll/setup does not exist, but the consequence the finding rests on is wrong: the firm-level PT state-coverage screen IS built, at apps/web/app/settings/statutory-values/page.tsx, linked from app/settings/page.tsx:711 and pinned by apps/web/scripts/statutory-values-record-what-was-read.test.ts. It lives under Settings rather than under /payroll/setup. What remains is that three payroll screens sit in no side panel and attendance sits under Team — an information-architecture shortfall against docs/architecture/10-payroll.md:131-147, with nothing unreachable and no capability missing. Downgraded to low.
verification.probe: grep -rn 'statutoryValues|statutory-values' over apps/web printed app/settings/statutory-values/page.tsx:84,143,185, app/settings/page.tsx:711 and scripts/statutory-values-record-what-was-read.test.ts — refuting 'no page calling them'. grep -n payroll lib/workspace/knownRoutes.generated.ts printed all six /payroll routes as known.

lens_notes.literal: The navigation facts hold: apps/web/components/panels/AccountingPanel.tsx:44-46 lists Payroll -> /payroll and Payroll Statutory -> /payroll/statutory; components/panels/TeamPanel.tsx:33 puts /payroll/attendance under Team; lib/workspace/workspaceConfig.ts:175 folds /payroll into the 'accounting' workspace; and a repo-wide grep for the three sub-routes outside app/payroll returns no panel entry, so /payroll/people, /payroll/declarations and /payroll/reports are reached only from the header buttons at app/payroll/page.tsx:933-946. app/payroll/ has no setup/ directory. BUT THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM IS FALSE. 'GET /statutory-values and PUT /statutory-values/pt exist in lib/api (index.ts:622-636) with no page calling them, so the firm-recorded-PT-slabs mechanism ... cannot be used' — the page exists: apps/web/app/settings/statutory-values/page.tsx:84,143,185 calls api.statutoryValues.list/savePtSlabs/removePtSlabs, and its header comment describes exactly the state-coverage function the finding says is unbuilt. It is linked from apps/web/app/settings/page.tsx:711 with copy naming the twenty-two/four split.
lens_notes.guards: apps/web/scripts/statutory-values-record-what-was-read.test.ts:44,63,100-101 asserts the settings link and the savePtSlabs call exist — a regression test pinning precisely the capability the finding calls missing. All six payroll routes are in lib/workspace/knownRoutes.generated.ts:108-113, so none is an orphan route. docs/architecture/10-payroll.md:131,147 does specify the 13th workspace and /payroll/setup, but the same document's status header (:12-32) declares the phase list stale and several items shipped since.
lens_notes.reach: Every screen the finding names is reachable by a real user: the three unpanelled ones from buttons on /payroll, state coverage from Settings, and the client-grain payroll workspace from lib/workspace/ClientNavContext.tsx:72. The design doc itself (:139) calls the client-scoped screen canonical for a payroll month, so the firm rail being a link rather than a rail costs navigation depth, not capability.

findings.title: The payslip omits UAN, PF/ESIC numbers, bank account, employer contributions and YTD figures
findings.evidence: services/payslip_pdf_service.py:118-238 renders: firm name, employee name/designation/department/PAN, pay period, working days / days present / LOP, seven earning lines plus one-time, five deduction lines, net pay. The employee master holds uan, esi_number, bank_account_no, bank_ifsc (models/payroll.py:63-67) and the slip holds pf_employer_paise, esi_employer_paise, edli_paise, pf_admin_paise — none reach the document. There is no YTD block and no net-pay-in-words.
findings.ca_experience: An employee querying their PF cannot find their UAN on the slip; an employee applying for a loan gets a payslip a bank will question because it names no employer registration and no bank account; and the employer's own contribution — which is what makes the CTC conversation possible — is invisible.
findings.market_standard: greytHR, Keka and Zoho payslips carry UAN, PF number, ESIC IP, bank account (masked), employer PF/ESI, YTD earnings and deductions, and net pay in words.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an employer block (from client + client_statutory_identity), an employee statutory block (UAN/ESIC/bank), an employer-contribution section and a YTD column. All the data is already on the slip and the master.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Confirmed and understated. services/payslip_pdf_service.py:116-238 omits UAN, ESIC number, bank account, employer contributions, YTD and net-in-words, and :256/:324 do not even select those columns. Beyond the finding: :116 with _load_firm at :372-381 prints the CA FIRM's name as the employer while run['client_id'] (selected at :256) is discarded, and _paise_to_rupee_str at :67-75 makes every amount render in ZapfDingbats as a black square because U+20B9 is absent from WinAnsiEncoding and no TTF is registered anywhere in apps/api. The same ₹-in-Helvetica pattern is in services/invoice_pdf_service.py:204,227, so it is not payslip-local. A document naming the wrong employer with unreadable currency is not a fine_tune — raised to high.

Extracted Tj tokens: 'Lobo and Co Chartered Accountants | Payslip for August 2026 | Asha Rao | Analyst | Dept: Audit | PAN: ABCDE1234F | Pay Period: | August 2026 | Working Days: | 30 | Days Present: | 30 | Earnings | Amount \( | n | \) | Basic | n | 25,000.00 | HRA | n | 10,000.00 | Gross Salary | n | 50,000.00 | Deductions | ... | Net Pay | n | 45,000.00 | This is a computer-generated payslip...'. '100200300400', '3100123456', '0011223344', 'HDFC0001234', 'UAN', 'YTD', 'Employer' all absent. Font objects in the PDF: 2 Helvetica/WinAnsi (F1), 3 Helvetica-Bold/WinAnsi (F2), 4 ZapfDingbats (F3) — and the 'n' beside every amount is drawn under /F3.

lens_notes.literal: Confirmed by rendering the document. services/payslip_pdf_service.py:116-238 emits exactly: employer name, 'Payslip for <Month Year>', employee name/designation/department/PAN, pay period + working days/days present/LOP, the earnings table, the deductions table (DEDUCTION_DEFS at :38-49 — PF employee, ESI employee, PT, TDS, loan recovery), Net Pay, and a boilerplate footer. No UAN, no ESIC number, no bank account, no employer contribution block, no YTD, no amount in words. The data is not merely unrendered — it is never LOADED: the employee join at :256 and :324 selects only (name, pan, designation, department), so uan/esi_number/bank_account_no/bank_ifsc from models/payroll.py:63-67 cannot reach the renderer even if a line were added. TWO DEFECTS THE FINDING MISSED, both worse than what it lists. (1) THE EMPLOYER NAMED IS THE WRONG ENTITY. :116 reads firm.get('name'), and firm comes from _load_firm(run['firm_id']) at :277/:329, which reads public.firms (:372-381) — the CA PRACTICE, the tenant. The employer is the CLIENT; run['client_id'] is selected at :256 and :315 and never used. Every payslip a bureau hands an employee is headed with the accountant's name. (2) THE RUPEE SIGN RENDERS AS A BLACK SQUARE. _paise_to_rupee_str (:67-75) embeds U+20B9, which is not in WinAnsiEncoding, so reportlab falls back per character to ZapfDingbats: the content stream is '/F3 10 Tf (n) Tj /F1 10 Tf (25,000.00) Tj' with /F3 resolving to '<< /BaseFont /ZapfDingbats /Name /F3 >>'. findings.title: UAN, ESIC number and IFSC are format-checked on bulk import but accepted unvalidated on the single create and update endpoints
findings.evidence: domain/payroll/employee_import.py:72-74 defines UAN_RE `^\d{12}$` and IFSC_RE `^[A-Z]{4}0[A-Z0-9]{6}$` and refuses the whole file on a mismatch (lines 278-286). models/payroll.py EmployeeIn/EmployeeUpdateIn validate only name, aadhaar_last4, pan and the percentages — uan, esi_number and bank_ifsc pass through untouched. domain/payroll/exceptions.py:74-121 catches them later, but only for clients with payroll_enabled and only if someone opens the Exceptions tab.
findings.ca_experience: A typo'd UAN entered on the form is accepted, sits on the master, and surfaces as an ECR refusal on the 15th — the exact round trip the exception index exists to prevent, and the import path already prevents.
findings.market_standard: Field-level validation at capture is universal.
findings.suggested_fix: Move UAN_RE / IFSC_RE (and a 10-digit ESIC check) into models/payroll.py as field validators shared with the importer, so one definition guards both doors.

verification.what_is_actually_true: Literally correct — one door validates UAN and IFSC (domain/payroll/employee_import.py:72-74, 279-287) and the other does not (models/payroll.py:63-67 with no field_validator for them; bound at routers/payroll.py:1292,1427), and ESIC number is unchecked on every path. The stated harm is overstated: domain/payroll/ecr.py:209-214 refuses a bad UAN at file build, so the failure surfaces locally rather than as an EPFO rejection, and domain/payroll/exceptions.py:73-122 already indexes it. Low is right, and the suggested fix (share the regexes into models/payroll.py) would give one definition for three doors.

maturity.rationale: This is the sharpest split in the codebase: a genuinely excellent statutory engine behind a surface that cannot reach half of it, plus a small number of wrong numbers that reach a CA. The engine deserves a B+/A- on its own — twenty-six domain modules, 743 passing payroll tests, §192 as a real projection with §192(3) adjustment, the three §115BAC objects kept apart, ESI Rule 50 contribution periods, the Code on Wages s.2(y) PF base with a period test, gratuity §4(2) at the day boundary, a named-gap discipline that refuses rather than guesses, and a release that blocks on unresolved gaps with a typed Partner override on a transition log. Almost nothing in the Indian market reasons this carefully. But the grade is what a CA would experience, and a CA would experience: an ECR whose wage column cannot reconcile with the contribution remitted (PAY-01), an Annexure II that gives old-regime employees the wrong §16(ia) and so produces a wrong Form 16 Part B (PAY-02), payslips headed with the accountant's name instead of the employer's (PAY-03), no way to settle a leaver or produce the year-end annexure from any screen (PAY-11), and no way to enter LOP from the client's own payroll tab (PAY-15). The owner's instinct about the client-workspace tab is correct and the evidence is specific: it has five well-designed verbs and the Inputs verb has no inputs in it. The docs are ahead of the code in two places that matter — the 1 September audit says the leaver is "wired" (the endpoint is; no screen calls it) and that the module can run a year (it cannot produce the year-end Annexure II from any screen).
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: Not yet — a CA could not run a full year on it today, because the leaver settlement, the salary revision, the employee advance and the Annexure II that becomes Form 16 exist only as endpoints with no screen, and the ECR they would upload on the 15th declares a wage the contribution does not reconcile to.

open_questions_for_owner: The 1 April 2027 cutover in docs/architecture/10-payroll.md rests on there being no mid-year opening-position import. Is that still the plan? If yes, PAY-04 (draft runs credited as TDS deducted) and PAY-21 (no way to recompute or discard a run) become urgent, because they are the two ways the first real month can go wrong with nothing on screen saying so. If the plan has moved to a mid-year start, `payroll_opening_positions` does not exist in any migration and the §192 projection withholds from a fiction.

Seven finished capabilities have no screen (PAY-11). Which order do you want them in? My reading of the calendar is Annexure II first (it is the year-end deliverable and June 2028 is the first hard date), then settlement, then salary revisions — but if the beachhead cohort has high churn, settlement is first.

The design doc says payroll becomes the 13th top-level workspace with a Setup screen that publishes PT/LWF state coverage. Neither exists, and the firm-recorded-PT-slabs endpoints (PUT /statutory-values/pt) have no caller. Is the state-coverage screen still the intended answer to the bundling problem, or has that been reconsidered?

The payslip currently carries the CA firm's name (PAY-03). Fixing it means deciding what a bureau payslip should say: employer only, or employer with a small 'processed by <firm>' line? That is a commercial decision, not a technical one.

Leave is half-built and the invented 12/12/15 defaults reach the employee portal (PAY-24). The design doc defers leave management. Do you want it removed until there is a policy model, or is a minimal per-client leave policy in scope?

Statutory bonus is computed only for leavers (PAY-23). Bonus is an annual obligation for every eligible employee under §19 of the Bonus Act. Is an annual bonus run in scope for the first cohort, or is the expectation that the CA does it outside the product for year one?

Two payroll deadline calendars exist, one in the backend compliance engine and one written in TypeScript on two payroll pages (PAY-19). The frontend one invents a professional-tax due date that compliance_engine deliberately refuses and that a test pins as absent. Do you want the payroll pages to render the engine's dates, or should payroll have no calendar of its own and point at /deadlines?

What is the realistic size of the first cohort — clients per firm, employees per client, months of history? PAY-16 (every slip of every run loaded into the browser) is harmless at seven clients and fatal at forty, and knowing the number decides whether that is a now-fix or a later-fix.

Is there an appetite for a small parity-test discipline between what the run computes and what each statutory file declares? PAY-01 and PAY-20 are both one implementation drifting from another, and the codebase already has the pattern (tests/test_cash_flow_sql_parity_pg.py, tests/test_schedule_iii_ageing_parity_pg.py) — it just was not applied to the ECR.
strengths: The §192 engine is genuinely ahead of the Indian market. routers/payroll.py:_months_employed_in_fy + _compute_slip project the year as what has actually been paid plus this month's rate times the months still to come, and _months_remaining_for_spread applies §192(3) against what THIS deductor has already withheld, degrading to annual/12 when there is no history — the docstring at line 1113 works through why counting from the calendar instead would double every payslip's TDS for a mid-year onboarding.

The three §115BAC objects are kept genuinely separate and nothing sets one from another. domain/payroll/declarations.py:1-70 distinguishes the Circular 04/2023 intimation (withholding), the §115BAC(6) election (the return, in domain/income_tax/regime_election.py) and the Rule 26C Form 12BB evidence, and `notices()` tells the CA that an old-regime intimation is not the election. Almost every payroll product conflates the first two.

The declared-versus-verified split is real and correctly gated. domain/payroll/declarations.py:DeclarationItem.effective_paise plus routers/payroll.py:PROOF_CUTOFF_MONTH_OF_FY=10 and _verified_only_from_month stop an unproved claim reducing tax from January, which is exactly where §192(1) liability bites; migration 297 enforces the same line in RLS so an employee filing through the portal cannot set a *_verified_paise column or proofs_verified.

The named-gap discipline is the module's best idea and it is applied consistently. _statutory_gaps, _attendance_gap, _age_gap and identity_domain.pt_registration_gaps all distinguish 'nothing is due' from 'something is due and nobody worked it out', and migration 328 turned that from advice into a block: finalize_run RECOMPUTES the gaps (routers/payroll.py:_release_gaps) so a CA who has since closed one is not still refused, and an override needs a 20-character typed reason on payroll_run_transitions.

The PF wage base under the Labour Codes is modelled properly and period-aware. domain/payroll/wage_base.py implements the Code on Wages s.2(y) proviso as a cap on exclusions with a deemed add-back, classifies only HRA (clause f) and LTA (clause d) as excluded with the reasoning for defaulting everything else to wages (citing RPFC v. Vivekananda Vidyamandir), reproduces the old basic+DA exactly for any month ending before 21-11-2025, and is pinned by 16 tests.

The EPS/EPF/EDLI/admin split is stored on the slip rather than recomputed, and the ₹500-per-establishment admin floor is applied on the run total rather than per payslip (domain/payroll/statutory.py:admin_charge_for_establishment, called from both create_run and statutory_position — moved, not copied). Migration 329 got EDLI and the admin charge into the general ledger.

ESI Rule 50 contribution periods are modelled, and the 'was this member covered when the period began' question is answered from payroll history rather than inferred from the current wage (routers/payroll.py:_members_contributing_earlier_this_period + domain/payroll/statutory.py:esi_contribution_period).

Gratuity is careful where it matters: domain/payroll/gratuity.py:completed_service compares by date so 'six months and one day' rounds the year up and six months exactly does not, the daily wage is one division rather than fifteen rounded ones, §4(2)'s 26-day divisor is used, and §10(10)'s lifetime limit is an input with a named gap rather than an assumption.

The statutory files refuse rather than guess, in the right places. domain/payroll/esic.py will not invent a reason code for a zero-wage member; domain/payroll/form24q.py refuses a deductee with no valid PAN because §206AA makes it a short deduction the employer carries; domain/payroll/ecr.py sanitises names against its own #~# delimiter so a name cannot shift the wage columns.

Attendance became a real contract. domain/payroll/attendance.py enforces days_present + paid leave + LOP = working_days and refuses an inconsistent row rather than flooring it, PUT /attendance writes only the employees sent, and migration 324's attendance_entered plus migration 326 mean 'confirmed full month' and 'nobody asked' are no longer the same row.

Tenancy and access are handled seriously on a sensitive surface: _assert_run_scope / _assert_employee_scope / _assert_slip_scope resolve payroll_slips (which has no firm_id) through its run, the firm-wide reads use filter_by_client so an Executive assigned to four clients cannot read forty clients' salaries, and migration 323 stops an employee reading a draft payslip in the RLS policy rather than in a page filter.

Test coverage on the engine is real: 743 payroll-related tests pass in mock mode across 33 test modules, including negative controls (the 1 September audit records mutating the code and requiring a named test to fail), a parity test holding the Python and SQL ageing implementations identical, and frontend guard tests (apps/web/scripts/statutory-files-are-server-built.test.ts) that stop the browser-built ECR coming back.
subsystem: Payroll — employee master, salary structures, attendance and leave, monthly runs, PF/ESI/PT/LWF, §192 TDS, declarations/Form 12BB/regime intimation, perquisites, §89 arrears, bonus, gratuity, leave encashment, full and final settlement, ECR/ESIC/24Q/Annexure II outputs, payslips, payroll journal posting, employee portal, firm-level payroll screens and the client-workspace Payroll tab
test_coverage_notes: Backend coverage is strong and unusually thoughtful. 743 payroll-related tests pass in mock mode (`pytest -k \"payroll or ecr or esic or 24q or gratuity or bonus or declar or settle or perquis or arrear or attendance or annexure or wage_base\"`, 9.1s, 99 real-Postgres tests self-skipping) across 33 modules. The domain modules are tested as arithmetic rather than through the router, which is why they are the reliable half: tests/test_the_pf_wage_base_under_the_labour_codes.py has 16 tests including the exact-50% boundary, the one-paise-over case, the commencement month itself and a pre-Code month reproducing basic+DA exactly; tests/test_gratuity.py, test_bonus_leave_and_settlement.py, test_it_declarations.py and test_perquisites.py each pin the statutory boundaries. Real-Postgres tests exist for the migrations that matter (297 declaration RLS, 323 draft payslips, 326 attendance constraints, 332 per-client enablement, 335 ECR filings). The frontend has genuine guard tests too — apps/web/scripts/statutory-files-are-server-built.test.ts stops the browser-built ECR returning, payroll-money-is-exact.test.ts guards the rupee parser, a-release-is-blocked-or-signed-for.test.ts guards the override.\n\nWhat is NOT tested is precisely where the findings are, and in three cases a test passes while the behaviour is wrong. (1) No test asserts that the ECR's EPF_WAGES reconciles against the contribution remitted — tests/test_epfo_ecr.py constructs ECRMember objects directly and never runs a slip through _compute_slip into build_ecr, which is why PAY-01 is green. (2) tests/test_24q_annexure_ii.py passes one STD_DEDUCTION constant and never parametrises the regime, so PAY-02 is green; the test at line 62 asserts the figure passed in, not the figure due. (3) apps/web/scripts/employee-form-captures-what-filing-needs.test.ts asserts joining_date is in the form and passes — while PATCH silently discards it (PAY-12), because the test reads the form file and never the model. (4) statutory-files-are-server-built.test.ts guards app/payroll/page.tsx only; app/payroll/reports/page.tsx still carries the browser-side employer PF/ESI it was written to eliminate (PAY-09). (5) No test covers _tds_already_deducted_this_fy's run-status filter, the loan write-down under reversal, the PT×12 annualisation or the ×12 HRA base. (6) Nothing tests the payslip PDF's employer identity. I found no test asserting a WRONG statutory rule — the tests are honest about what they check; the gap is that they check the domain modules and not the seams between them.
what_exists: Backend. `routers/payroll.py` (5,902 lines) exposes ~55 endpoints over 26 domain modules in `domain/payroll/`. Employee master with bulk import (`employee_import.py`, whole-file validation, idempotent on `employee_code`, migration 333) and a CSV template. Salary structures (migration 054) that are applied by writing a `payroll_salary_revisions` row (migration 300) rather than a live link, with per-employee drift reported where the stored two-decimal HRA percentage cannot reproduce the intended figure. Attendance as a server-side contract (`attendance.py`, migration 326) enforcing days_present + paid leave + LOP = working_days, with absence of a row meaning \"not entered\". One-time and variable earnings (migration 331) carrying their own PF/ESI/taxable flags derived from EPF §2(b), ESI §2(22)'s two-month interval test and §17(1)(iv). Monthly runs: `create_run` hoists every read out of the per-employee loop, merges any revision in force over the master, computes each slip in integer paise, and returns `statutory_gaps` and `attendance_gaps` with the run. `_compute_slip` prorates on working_days − lop_days, computes the PF base through `wage_base.compute` (Code on Wages s.2(y), effective 21-11-2025), splits the employer 12% into EPS/EPF with EDLI and admin charge, applies ESI with Rule 50 contribution periods, computes PT for MH/TN/KA/WB in code and other states from firm-recorded slabs (migration 327), and withholds §192 on a real projection with the §192(3) adjustment. Release is a three-step lifecycle: `PATCH /status`, `POST /finalize` (recomputes gaps, blocks or takes a 20-character Partner override onto `payroll_run_transitions`, posts through the one journal kernel dated to the month end, then writes down loan balances), `POST /disburse`, `POST /reverse`. Statutory outputs are all server-built: EPFO ECR (`ecr.py` + `ecr_sequence.py` + migration 335's filing record and blocking-month logic), the ESIC contribution CSV, the 24Q deductee source and CSV working paper, and 24Q Q4 Annexure II. Leavers: `settlement.py` composes gratuity, leave encashment and bonus onto the correct §17 lines, withholds under §192, posts through the kernel and closes the employee. Also: §89/Form 10E, Rule 3 perquisites, employee loans, per-client statutory identity (migration 325), per-client payroll enablement (migration 332), a firm-wide client-month queue and a firm-wide exception index. Payslip PDFs single and as a run zip.\n\nFrontend. `/payroll` (995 lines) — a client-month queue plus a statutory-returns checklist; `/payroll/people` (roster + exceptions); `/payroll/attendance` (1,278, attendance + one-time earnings, reached from the Team rail); `/payroll/declarations` (483); `/payroll/statutory` (398, server-computed); `/payroll/reports` (1,354, entirely browser-computed); `/clients/[id]/payroll` (1,995) with tabs Inputs · Register · Release · Outputs · Setup; and an employee portal with payslips, leave balances and a tax-declaration tab.
